market_summary:
US equities staged a sharp one-day rebound (S&P +2.35%, Nasdaq +2.74%) on Nov 9 after a rough October for mega-cap tech, but the move looks more like a short-covering bounce than a trend change given NVDA, GOOGL and META are all still deeply negative over 1-3 months. Nvidia is under a fresh political/legal cloud (CEO Jensen Huang reportedly under investigation over alleged China ties, stock -4% on Nov 9) just a week before its Nov 17 earnings, adding event risk on top of an already-battered chart (-22.5% 1m, -25% from 52w high). In Singapore, Q3 bank earnings were mixed — OCBC beat while DBS and UOB missed — yet all three sold off together over the past week, creating a potential dislocation between OCBC's relative fundamental strength and its price. Singtel reports earnings Nov 13 with unusually strong analyst conviction (13 buy/2 hold, 28% implied upside) despite the stock sitting near 52-week lows, setting up a binary but interesting long into the print.</market_summary>
